plan.melodySummary: The melody emerges from silence in the Cello's low register, then rises through Tenor Sax and Oboe as the texture thins and swells subtly at the central climax before the English Horn carries it back down into darkness. The dynamic arc floats between !pp! and !mp!, with a single restrained swell near mm.13-18 before dissolving into an unresolved whisper.

sections.label: Phrase A — Emergence
sections.notes: Play unaccompanied at !pp!, dark and searching in the low-middle register; let the opening rest breathe and leave the phrase ends hanging.

sections.label: Phrase A' — First Color
sections.notes: Take the melody at !pp!-!p!, breathy and veiled; Cello enters only on sustained low open fifths beneath you, never louder than the tune.

sections.label: Phrase B — Central Swell
sections.notes: Carry the melody at !mp! — the piece's high point — with a single controlled swell; stay above the English Horn's chromatic neighbor-tone shadow and the Cello's low pedal.

sections.label: Phrase B' — Descent into Dark
sections.notes: Return to !pp!, sinking and mournful; hold the final Am (m.24) barely audible over the Cello's low fifth, leaving it unresolved and dissolving into silence.

Oboe.instruction: Silent until the central Phrase B; then carry the melody at !mp! with a lone swell, the only moment of light before receding to tacet.

English Horn.instruction: In mm.13-18 add a !pp! chromatic-neighbor countermelody under the Oboe; in mm.19-24 take the main melody at !pp!, dark and unresolved, fading into silence.

Tenor Sax.instruction: Enter as the melody's first color-shift at !pp!-!p!, breathy and low; tacet elsewhere so its single appearance feels like a shadow emerging.

Cello.instruction: Open the piece alone in a dark low register at !pp!; from mm.7 onward drop to sustained open fifths and minor pedal tones, always softer than whoever holds the tune.
